title: Secure build, test, and release supply chains
question: Which linked identities, digests, attestations, tests, and approvals justify promoting this exact artifact, and which claim fails when one link changes?
scenario: A pipeline can deploy any file placed in an artifact bucket, and SAST findings are merely reported.
focalRelation: approved source revision and dependency lock --inputs--> isolated builder identity builder --recorded steps and tests--> artifact digest signing identity --attests named claim; signature alone does not prove safety--> artifact promotion identity --verifies digest, provenance, policy and approval--> repository/target runtime observation and rollback --operational evidence--> release decision

nodes.label: Approved source commit
nodes.detail: Reviewed source and dependency manifest identified by immutable revision.

nodes.label: Isolated build identity
nodes.detail: Ephemeral, least-privilege builder with protected inputs, environment, and no standing production access.

nodes.label: Signed provenance statement
nodes.detail: Attestation binding source, dependencies, builder identity, process, artifact digest, and time.

nodes.label: Security test evidence
nodes.detail: SAST, SCA, DAST, and IAST results with scope, disposition, exceptions, and retest status.

nodes.label: Promotion gate
nodes.detail: Policy verifies provenance, artifact digest, approvals, tests, and target before promotion.

nodes.label: Production artifact
nodes.detail: Exact verified artifact deployed through bounded authority, monitoring, and rollback.

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: A pipeline can deploy any file placed in an artifact bucket, and SAST findings are merely reported.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: A compromised runner can alter every downstream artifact.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: A clean SAST report proves the release is secure. It cannot cover runtime configuration, dependency provenance, deployment identity, or all dynamic and business-logic abuse.

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Restrict artifact writes, sign or attest provenance, verify identity at promotion, bind deployment to approved commit and test evidence, triage high-risk findings, and provide rollback. The goal is a trustworthy release path, not a dashboard of scans.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Design layered pipeline controls that produce trustworthy, traceable release artifacts. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

variants.label: Changed case
variants.changedFact: A dependency is republished under a valid-looking signature from a compromised but previously trusted publisher identity, and affected versions may already be deployed.

states.title: Changed case fact isolated
states.caption: A dependency is republished under a valid-looking signature from a compromised but previously trusted publisher identity, and affected versions may already be deployed.

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Affected promotion is frozen while build and deployment records identify prior artifacts; trusted publisher and integrity policy are revalidated before a clean rebuild.

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

prediction.prompt: An artifact has a valid signature and clean SAST result, but its builder identity is unapproved and no record ties its digest to the reviewed source revision. Promote it?

options.label: No; bind this digest to approved source, builder, tests, signer, and approval
options.feedback: Correct. The promotion identity must verify the linked evidence for this exact artifact.

options.label: Yes; signature plus SAST proves it is trustworthy.
options.feedback: A signature attests a signer-controlled claim and SAST covers bounded code patterns; neither repairs missing builder/source provenance.

options.label: Deploy first and use runtime monitoring as provenance evidence.
options.feedback: Monitoring supports operation and response; it does not establish where the artifact came from.

prediction.hint: Name the controlling relationship and the point where its result must be enforced; do not rely on a label or successful prior step.

transfer.prompt: A dependency is republished under a valid-looking signature from a compromised but previously trusted publisher identity, and affected versions may already be deployed.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: A dependency is republished under a valid-looking signature from a compromised but previously trusted publisher identity, and affected versions may already be deployed. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Restrict artifact writes, sign or attest provenance, verify identity at promotion, bind deployment to approved commit and test evidence, triage high-risk findings, and provide rollback. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Affected promotion is frozen while build and deployment records identify prior artifacts; trusted publisher and integrity policy are revalidated before a clean rebuild.

options.label: Freeze affected promotion, trace builds and deployments from dependency/build records
options.feedback: Correct. Freeze affected promotion, trace builds and deployments from dependency/build records, validate trusted publisher and integrity policy, rebuild in a clean runner from approved inputs, rotate affected credentials as warranted, and investigate prior artifacts.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: A dependency is republished under a valid-looking signature from a compromised but previously trusted publisher identity, and affected versions may already be deployed. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Restrict artifact writes, sign or attest provenance, verify identity at promotion, bind deployment to approved commit and test evidence, triage high-risk findings, and provide rollback. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: SCA finds a vulnerable component with no reachable exploit path, while a critical DAST authorization flaw is open. Which response is best?

options.label: Proceed on the assumption that a clean SAST report proves the release is secure
options.feedback: That repeats the key misconception. It cannot cover runtime configuration, dependency provenance, deployment identity, or all dynamic and business-logic abuse.

options.label: Accept the visible success signal and defer scope, owner, exception, and evidence checks until later
options.feedback: The visible signal does not establish Production artifact. Tool severity is not the same as business risk.

options.label: Rank both findings by exposure, reachability, and business consequence
options.feedback: Correct. Tool severity is not the same as business risk.

retry.hint: Identify what changed, who owns the resulting decision, and what evidence would demonstrate the bounded outcome.

takeaway: Restrict artifact writes, sign or attest provenance, verify identity at promotion, bind deployment to approved commit and test evidence, triage high-risk findings, and provide rollback.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The state graph preserves immutable source, isolated build identity, signed provenance, security evidence, promotion authority, production digest, dependency-compromise response, and rollback ownership. Learners inspect authored gate states rather than independently toggling every reviewed build/release gate, so the mechanism is equivalent.

learningJob.plainExplanation: A signature or clean scan alone does not prove an artifact is trustworthy. Promotion should bind the exact digest to approved source, builder identity, dependencies, tests, signer, approval, and rollback evidence.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The provenance chain allows the learner to trace one exact artifact backward through digest, builder, source, dependency, tests, signer, and approval before promotion.
